Theme 030 · Material & 3D

Stitch & Thread

Metrics are cross-stitched in teal thread on oat linen, and a silver needle is the agent working quietly in the background. A wrong stitch is unpicked in coral with a seam ripper, and the human approves the re-stitch with a sewn-on button.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Weave ground — oat linen texture from two fine repeating gradients
  • Stitch cell — two diagonal thread strokes + a highlight — one data pixel
  • Needle + running thread — the agent: a silver sliver leading each row, trailing a thread path
  • Seam ripper — the anomaly tool; pulls out the coral stitches
  • Sewn label — fabric tag with a dashed stitch border for the anomaly details
  • Sewn button — a four-hole button on a fabric tag — the human action

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Stitch-reveal — per-cell stroke-dashoffset on steps() at 12 fps, 0.03 s stagger; a row completes every beat at 120 BPM
  • Needle bob — 0.15 s sine up/down ahead of the stitch front, locked to sixteenth notes
  • Unpick — coral thread pulls out with power2.in 0.3 s on the snare, then re-stitches teal over the next bar

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Embroidery reads as meticulous care — exactly what “checking every metric” should feel like — and unpick-and-restitch gives a clean error → fix beat that is highly distinctive in a feed. Risk: stitched digits get noisy; keep stitched numbers large and few and set exact values as typeset labels.

Adapt to your product: Stitch your product's key chart or icon grid, let your agent be the needle, and turn the one thing it catches into the coral stitches that get unpicked; primary actions become sewn buttons.
